items.toString: This work item links to "openshift/installer#10625: CORS-4507: aws: support edge machine pool management with ClusterAPI (Web Link)"

items.fromString:
h2. User Story:

When edge machine pool set {{Cluster API}} as the management mode, the installer should produce {{MachineSet}} and {{InfrastructureTemplate}} manifests. Edge machine manifests are different from regular worker’s in the following ways:

* Node taints should be applied to edge nodes to prevent regular workloads to schedule on them. This requires taint support on CAPI machines, which propagate to nodes.
* Helper labels should be applied on edge nodes for customers to schedule their “edge” workload based on zone-type, zone-group, and parent zone criteria.
** {{machine.openshift.io/parent-zone-name: <value_of_ParentZoneName>}}
** {{machine.openshift.io/zone-group: <value_of_ZoneGroup>}}
** {{machine.openshift.io/zone-type: <value_of_ZoneType>}}

h2. Acceptance Criteria:

Description of criteria:

* Appropriate Edge Compute Manifests are produced (no MAPI)
* Edge compute Nodes are provisioned day-2

h2. (optional) Out of Scope:

N/A

h2. Engineering Details:

* See details in [enhancement|https://github.com/openshift/enhancements/blob/master/enhancements/machine-api/converting-machine-api-to-cluster-api.md#machineset-synchronisation]

h2. Testing Details:

* Separate jobs should be created to enable specifying CAPI compute at install time
* We should maximally specify the configuration, to minimize testing cardinality
* Check with cloud team to see if we can depend on their tests

(?) This requires/does not require a design proposal.
(?) This requires/does not require a feature gate.

This work item links to "openshift/release#79851: CORS-4502: aws: update bastion AMI and mirror images for C2S/SC2S (Web Link)"

h2. Problems

The C2S/SC2S bastion host AMI ({{ami-0fba1e74cafe37fa8}}) used in disconnected CI jobs is running RHEL 7.6 (EOL) with Docker registry v2 ([docker.io/library/registry:2|http://docker.io/library/registry:2]). Furthermore, related mirror images are hosted under a personal namespace [http://quay.io/yunjiang|http://quay.io/yunjiang/], for example, [https://github.com/openshift/release/blob/9db451076e61c925819602ed42845a1d44818b90/ci-operator/step-registry/aws/c2s/mirror-images/aws-c2s-mirror-images-commands.sh#L39|https://github.com/openshift/release/blob/9db451076e61c925819602ed42845a1d44818b90/ci-operator/step-registry/aws/c2s/mirror-images/aws-c2s-mirror-images-commands.sh#L39|smart-link]

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. *Migrate C2S mirror images to* {{openshift-install}} *namespace:*

Replace personal {{quay.io/yunjiang/}} references with {{quay.io/openshift-install/}}   in the C2S provisioning steps:

* c2s-instance-metadata:latest
* cap-token-refresh:latest

h3. *Rebuild bastion host AMI on RHEL 10:*

Replace the bastion host AMI with a new RHEL 10-based image.

* OS: RHEL 7.6 → RHEL 10
* Registry: [http://docker.io/library/registry:2|http://docker.io/library/registry:2]  (env var config) → [http://quay.io/openshifttest/registry:3|http://quay.io/openshifttest/registry:3]
* Other services such as squid proxy, httpd need to be preserved with minor updates to work on RHEL 10.
* I already built one based on the current bastion host running CI: {{ami-0cfa565a0a200d2c7}}

so that I can achieve

h2. Engineering Details:

* MAPI currently has a for loop that assumes the frontend ip configs is equal to the backend pools. This causes an error when the installer creates multiple backend pools for v4 and v6 for inbound and outbound while frontend ip config falls short in the count.

items.fromString:
h2. Summary

{{pkg/asset/cluster/tfvars/tfvars.go}} calls {{workersAsset.MachineSets()}} for multiple platforms and extracts MAPI provider specs into {{WorkerConfigs}}, but the generated tfvars data is never consumed downstream. One active reference to worker machinesets exists outside of tfvars in the OpenStack CAPI PreProvision hook, which needs refactoring.

h2. Unused worker machineset references (remove)

The following platforms generate {{WorkerConfigs}} from MAPI worker machinesets and write them to tfvars, but no infrastructure code reads the worker-derived fields:

* *AWS* ({{tfvars.go:278-286}}): Extracts {{AWSMachineProviderConfig}} → {{WorkerConfigs}} → {{awstfvars.TFVars}} computes worker availability zones. AWS CAPI ignition never reads {{TFVarsAsset}}.
* *Azure* ({{tfvars.go:377-384}}): Extracts {{AzureMachineProviderSpec}} → {{WorkerConfigs}} → {{azuretfvars.TFVars}} sets {{ComputeSubnet}}. Azure CAPI ignition never reads {{TFVarsAsset}}.
* *GCP* ({{tfvars.go:486-504}}): Extracts {{GCPMachineProviderSpec}} → {{WorkerConfigs}} → {{gcptfvars.TFVars}} sets {{ComputeSubnet}}. GCP CAPI reads {{TFVarsAsset}} but only for {{gcp_ignition_shim}}, which is not derived from worker machinesets.
* *IBM Cloud* ({{tfvars.go:603-609}}): Extracts {{IBMCloudMachineProviderSpec}} → {{WorkerConfigs}} → {{ibmcloudtfvars.TFVars}} sets worker zones/subnets. IBM Cloud CAPI ignition never reads {{TFVarsAsset}}.
* *OpenStack* ({{tfvars.go:750-766}}): Passes {{workersAsset}} to {{openstacktfvars.TFVars}}, which extracts {{WorkerServerGroupNames}}. Output is only consumed by {{ReplaceBootstrapIgnitionInTFVars}}, which is gated behind {{!capiutils.IsEnabled()}} — always false.
* *oVirt* ({{tfvars.go:786-842}}): Entire oVirt case is dead code — no infrastructure provider registered in {{ProviderForPlatform()}}. Uses {{mastersAsset.Machines()}} only, but the whole block is unused.

h3. What to remove

# Remove {{workersAsset.MachineSets()}} calls and {{WorkerConfigs}} extraction from the AWS, Azure, GCP, IBM Cloud cases in {{tfvars.go}}
# Remove {{WorkerConfigs}} field from {{TFVarsSources}} structs in {{pkg/tfvars/aws/aws.go}}, {{pkg/tfvars/azure/azure.go}}, {{pkg/tfvars/gcp/gcp.go}}, {{pkg/tfvars/ibmcloud/ibmcloud.go}}
# Remove worker-config-derived logic from each platform's {{TFVars()}} function (worker availability zones in AWS, {{ComputeSubnet}} in GCP/Azure, worker zones/subnets in IBM Cloud)
# Remove the {{workersAsset}} parameter from {{openstacktfvars.TFVars}} and the worker spec extraction within it
# Remove the entire oVirt case from {{tfvars.go}} and the {{ovirttfvars}} package usage
# Remove {{&machines.Worker{}}} from {{TerraformVariables.Dependencies()}} if no remaining cases need it
# Clean up unused imports ({{machinev1beta1}}, {{ovirtprovider}}, {{ibmcloudprovider}}, etc.)

h2. Active reference requiring refactoring

*OpenStack CAPI PreProvision* ({{pkg/infrastructure/openstack/clusterapi/clusterapi.go:99-112}}):

{code:go}machineSets, err := workersAsset.MachineSets()
for _, machineSet := range machineSets {
    workerSpecs = append(workerSpecs, *machineSet.Spec.Template.Spec.ProviderSpec.Value.Object.(*mapov1alpha1.OpenstackProviderSpec))
}
preprovision.ServerGroups(ctx, installConfig, capiMachines, workerSpecs){code}

This extracts {{ServerGroupName}} from each worker machineset's {{OpenstackProviderSpec}} to pre-create server groups. This value can be derived from the install config's worker machine pool ({{installConfig.Config.Compute[].Platform.OpenStack}}) combined with the infra ID, without requiring MAPI machinesets.

h3. Refactoring steps

# Update {{preprovision.ServerGroups()}} to accept worker server group info derived from the install config instead of {{[]mapov1alpha1.OpenstackProviderSpec}}
# Remove {{WorkersAsset}} from {{PreProvisionInput}} in {{pkg/infrastructure/clusterapi/types.go}} (if no other platform uses it)
# Remove {{workersAsset}} from {{clusterapi.go}} {{Provision()}} if no longer needed

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* All unused {{WorkerConfigs}} / {{MachineSets()}} references removed from tfvars generation
* Dead oVirt tfvars case removed
* OpenStack server group creation works from install config data instead of MAPI worker machinesets
* No regression in any platform's infrastructure provisioning
* Unit tests updated to reflect removed parameters
items.toString:
h2. Summary

The {{TerraformVariables}} asset ({{pkg/asset/cluster/tfvars/tfvars.go}}) and the entire {{pkg/tfvars/}} package tree generate platform-specific Terraform variable files that are no longer consumed by infrastructure provisioning. Only two consumers remain: GCP CAPI reads a single field ({{gcp_ignition_shim}}), and baremetal reads config values from disk — both can be trivially refactored. Everything else is dead code.

This story removes the entire tfvars layer rather than selectively pruning it.

h2. What to remove

h3. Dead tfvars generation

The following platform cases in {{tfvars.go}} generate {{MasterConfigs}} and/or {{WorkerConfigs}} from MAPI machine manifests. No downstream infrastructure code reads the output:

* *AWS* ({{tfvars.go:270-353}}): Generates master/worker {{AWSMachineProviderConfig}} → {{awstfvars.TFVars}}. AWS CAPI never reads {{TFVarsAsset}}.
* *Azure* ({{tfvars.go:354-444}}): Generates master/worker {{AzureMachineProviderSpec}} → {{azuretfvars.TFVars}}. Azure CAPI never reads {{TFVarsAsset}}.
* *IBM Cloud* ({{tfvars.go:584-749}}): Generates master/worker {{IBMCloudMachineProviderSpec}} → {{ibmcloudtfvars.TFVars}}. IBM Cloud CAPI never reads {{TFVarsAsset}}.
* *OpenStack* ({{tfvars.go:750-766}}): Passes workers to {{openstacktfvars.TFVars}}. Output only consumed by {{ReplaceBootstrapIgnitionInTFVars}}, gated behind {{!capiutils.IsEnabled()}} — always false.
* *oVirt* ({{tfvars.go:786-842}}): Entire case is dead code — no infrastructure provider registered in {{ProviderForPlatform()}}.
* *Nutanix* ({{tfvars.go:849-881}}): Generates master {{NutanixMachineProviderConfig}} → {{nutanixtfvars.TFVars}}. Nutanix CAPI never reads {{TFVarsAsset}}.
* *PowerVS / vSphere* ({{tfvars.go:843-848}}): Already return early with empty file lists.

h3. Packages to delete

* {{pkg/tfvars/}} (base package — {{tfvars.go}} with {{Config}} struct and {{TFVars()}} func)
* {{pkg/tfvars/aws/}}
* {{pkg/tfvars/azure/}}
* {{pkg/tfvars/gcp/}}
* {{pkg/tfvars/ibmcloud/}}
* {{pkg/tfvars/openstack/}}
* {{pkg/tfvars/ovirt/}}
* {{pkg/tfvars/nutanix/}}
* {{pkg/tfvars/baremetal/}}
* {{pkg/asset/cluster/tfvars/}} (the {{TerraformVariables}} asset itself)

h3. Struct/field removal

* Remove {{TFVarsAsset}} from {{IgnitionInput}} in {{pkg/infrastructure/clusterapi/types.go}}
* Remove {{tfvarsAsset}} from CAPI {{Provision()}} in {{pkg/infrastructure/clusterapi/clusterapi.go}}
* Remove {{TerraformVariables}} from {{Cluster}} asset dependencies in {{pkg/asset/cluster/cluster.go}}
* Remove {{WorkersAsset}} from {{PreProvisionInput}} in {{pkg/infrastructure/clusterapi/types.go}} (after OpenStack refactor)

h2. Consumers requiring refactoring

h3. GCP CAPI — small (~10 lines)

{{pkg/infrastructure/gcp/clusterapi/clusterapi.go:140-155}} reads {{gcp_ignition_shim}} from tfvars. This shim is a bootstrap ignition pointer generated from a presigned GCS URL.

GCP CAPI already creates the bucket in {{Ignition()}}. Refactor to also generate the signed URL and shim inline using {{gcpbootstrap.CreateSignedURL()}} + {{bootstrap.GenerateIgnitionShimWithCertBundleAndProxy()}}, eliminating the tfvars dependency.

h3. Baremetal — moderate

{{pkg/infrastructure/baremetal/}} reads {{terraform.tfvars.json}} and {{terraform.platform.auto.tfvars.json}} from disk via {{getConfig(dir)}} in {{variables.go}}. It extracts {{ClusterID}}, {{IgnitionBootstrap}}, {{LibvirtURI}}, {{FIPS}}, {{ReleaseImagePullSpec}}, {{PullSecret}}, {{MirrorConfig}}, and {{Bridges}}.

All values originate from install config + bootstrap ignition + release image assets. Refactor {{Provision()}} and {{DestroyBootstrap()}} to get values from {{parents.Get()}} instead of the disk round-trip through tfvars. The {{baremetalConfig}} struct can remain, just populated directly from assets.

h3. OpenStack CAPI PreProvision — moderate

{{pkg/infrastructure/openstack/clusterapi/clusterapi.go:99-112}} calls {{workersAsset.MachineSets()}} to extract {{ServerGroupName}} from each worker machineset's MAPI {{OpenstackProviderSpec}}. This is the only _actively used_ MAPI machineset reference in the infrastructure layer.

Refactor {{preprovision.ServerGroups()}} to derive worker server group names from the install config's worker machine pool ({{installConfig.Config.Compute[].Platform.OpenStack}}) combined with the infra ID, without requiring MAPI machinesets.

Note: {{pkg/tfvars/openstack}} also exports {{GetServerGroupPolicy()}} which is used by {{preprovision/servergroups.go}}. This helper should be relocated to the preprovision package or an openstack utilities package before deleting {{pkg/tfvars/openstack/}}.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* {{TerraformVariables}} asset and all {{pkg/tfvars/}} packages removed
* GCP CAPI generates ignition shim inline
* Baremetal populates config from assets instead of tfvars files on disk
* OpenStack server group creation derives worker info from install config
* {{TFVarsAsset}} and {{WorkersAsset}} removed from CAPI infrastructure types
* No regression in any platform's infrastructure provisioning
* Unit tests updated
